items.title: CVE-2026-71885 (CRITICAL 9.2): In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, the Messaging Layer Security (MLS, RFC 9420) implementation did not bi…
items.one_liner: Critical crypto vulnerability in Bouncy Castle Java's MLS implementation allows credential spoofing and impersonation.
items.summary: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, the Messaging Layer Security implementation failed to properly bind X.509 credentials to a LeafNode's signature_key. Because the implementation stored the certificate chain without validating it or requiring the end-entity certificate's public key to match the signature key per RFC 9420, an attacker could present another party's certificate as its credential while signing with an unrelated key. This flaw allowed an unauthenticated attacker in certain deployments to be admitted under a victim's identity, evict the victim, decrypt group messages, and impersonate them. TreeKEM.LeafNode now strictly requires the end-entity certificate's subject public key to equal signature_key for X.509 credentials, rejecting non-matching leaves.
items.bottom_line: Update Bouncy Castle for Java to version 1.86 immediately to prevent MLS credential spoofing and group impersonation attacks.

items.title: The Model Plants the Trigger: Answer-Side Backdoor Attacks in Multi-Turn Large Language Models
items.one_liner: Multi-turn LLMs are vulnerable to answer-side backdoors where a self-generated dialogue word acts as a trigger, bypassing input-centric guardrails and safety refusals.
items.summary: Safety alignment in multi-turn large language models is vulnerable to a novel answer-side backdoor attack that bypasses input-centric guardrails. Instead of injecting a trigger into user inputs, the adversary uses a benign first-turn prompt to induce the model to generate a seemingly innocuous trigger word that becomes part of the dialogue history. When a later harmful query is processed, the model detects this self-generated trigger and bypasses safety refusals while keeping the user input completely clean. Experiments across four LLMs show near-perfect attack success rates at a low poisoning rate while evading standard defenses through representation-level refusal suppression.
items.bottom_line: Input-centric guardrails fail against answer-side backdoors in multi-turn LLMs where self-generated dialogue words act as triggers to suppress safety refusals.

items.title: When to Remember, When to Abstain: Category-Conditioned Retention for Reliable Agent Memory
items.one_liner: Category-conditioned retention thresholds improve LLM agent memory reliability by filtering out unsupported value and belief assertions.
items.summary: Persistent agent memory systems often suffer from reliability issues because weak assertions are stored and later treated as established facts. Researchers study whether retention decisions should use a category-conditioned confidence threshold rather than a single global bar, keeping well-evidenced categories while abstaining on unreliable inferences. An empirical evaluation across 4,715 candidate assertions revealed a reliability asymmetry where only 77.9% of value and belief assertions are source-supported compared to 96.2% for other categories. Implementing a stricter category-conditioned threshold on values reduced unsupported retentions from 6.2% to 4.0% while preserving estimation coverage. This approach demonstrates that reliable memory retention depends on semantic category and can serve as effective selective prediction at the write boundary.
items.bottom_line: Using semantic category-conditioned thresholds instead of a global confidence bar significantly reduces unsupported memory retentions in LLM agents.

items.title: Understanding and Mitigating Inference-Time Overreliance Using Agentic Memory
items.one_liner: MEMTRIM is a new plug-and-play framework that prevents LLM agents from relying on misleading or conflicting retrieved memories.
items.summary: Agentic memory allows LLM agents to reuse past experience, but retrieved memories can distort inference due to partial query-memory overlap, a failure mode known as memory overreliance. To mitigate this without model retraining, researchers propose MEMTRIM, a plug-and-play framework that indexes memory at write time and controls reuse at read time. MEMTRIM eliminates repeated or conflicting evidence while retaining useful information across both embedding-based and structured memory architectures. Experiments confirm that the framework reduces memory overreliance while preserving the utility of past agent experiences.
items.bottom_line: The MEMTRIM framework successfully mitigates LLM agent memory overreliance by filtering conflicting and redundant memory evidence at read and write time.

items.title: Efficient Auditing of Adversarial AI Agent Behavior from Agent Traces
items.one_liner: A two-stage auditing framework reduces LLM agent monitoring costs and token usage while effectively catching adversarial behavior.
items.summary: LLM-powered AI agents can perform complex tasks but may introduce security risks through unauthorized actions. Traditional guardrails either rely on rigid rules that can be bypassed or use costly continuous LLM monitoring for every action. To resolve this, researchers developed a two-stage auditing framework that uses lightweight gate rules to flag suspicious pending actions, followed by an LLM audit agent that inspects them within the agent's prior trace context. Tested on public benchmarks, the framework reduces average LLM audit frequency and token usage by over 70% while maintaining high malicious trace detection rates.
items.bottom_line: Combining deterministic gate rules with targeted LLM trace inspections reduces safety auditing token consumption by over 70% without sacrificing detection efficacy.
